text: The core of electronic information engineering is "achieving the acquisition, transmission, processing and application of information through electronic technology". It takes "signals" as the core research object - including electrical signals, optical signals, radio frequency signals, etc. Through designing electronic circuits, developing communication systems, and building information processing algorithms, it addresses issues related to efficiency, accuracy and reliability in information transmission. For example, during a phone call, the voice is first converted into an electrical signal, then encoded and modulated before being transmitted via radio waves. At the receiving end, it is decoded and restored to sound. Every step of this process falls within the scope of research in electronic information engineering.
